records.student_text: Zoe walks toward the front of a train moving east at 9 m/s. Zoe walks at 2 m/s relative to the train. Explain how Zoe can be moving relative to the ground while also being described using a different motion relative to the train.
records.student_html:
Zoe walks toward the front of a train moving east at 9 m/s. Zoe walks at 2 m/s relative to the train. Explain how Zoe can be moving relative to the ground while also being described using a different motion relative to the train.

  1. Reference frames change the object’s mass, which changes its motion.
  2. Relative to the train, Zoe moves east at 2 m/s; relative to the ground, Zoe moves east at 11 m/s. Motion depends on the chosen reference frame.
  3. Zoe must have the same velocity in every reference frame.
  4. Zoe is at rest relative to the ground because the train is the only valid frame.
choices: Reference frames change the object’s mass, which changes its motion.
Relative to the train, Zoe moves east at 2 m/s; relative to the ground, Zoe moves east at 11 m/s. Motion depends on the chosen reference frame.
Zoe must have the same velocity in every reference frame.
Zoe is at rest relative to the ground because the train is the only valid frame.
records.answer: Relative to the train, Zoe moves east at 2 m/s; relative to the ground, Zoe moves east at 11 m/s. Motion depends on the chosen reference frame.
records.solution_text: Use one reference frame at a time. The train-frame motion is the walking speed; the ground-frame motion combines the train motion and walking motion because both are east.
records.solution_html: Use one reference frame at a time. The train-frame motion is the walking speed; the ground-frame motion combines the train motion and walking motion because both are east.

records.student_text: A passenger on a bus says a phone on the seat is at rest. A person on the sidewalk says the phone is moving east with the bus. Compare the two descriptions and explain why using Earth’s surface is convenient for ordinary travel descriptions.
records.student_html:
A passenger on a bus says a phone on the seat is at rest. A person on the sidewalk says the phone is moving east with the bus. Compare the two descriptions and explain why using Earth’s surface is convenient for ordinary travel descriptions.

  1. Only the passenger can be correct because the phone is touching the seat.
  2. Only the sidewalk observer can be correct because Earth is the unique true frame.
  3. Both must measure zero velocity because the phone is not sliding.
  4. Both descriptions can be correct because they use different reference frames. The phone is at rest in the bus frame and moving in the Earth/sidewalk frame. Earth’s surface is a convenient shared everyday frame.
choices: Only the passenger can be correct because the phone is touching the seat.
Only the sidewalk observer can be correct because Earth is the unique true frame.
Both must measure zero velocity because the phone is not sliding.

Both descriptions can be correct because they use different reference frames. The phone is at rest in the bus frame and moving in the Earth/sidewalk frame. Earth’s surface is a convenient shared everyday frame.
records.answer: Both descriptions can be correct because they use different reference frames. The phone is at rest in the bus frame and moving in the Earth/sidewalk frame. Earth’s surface is a convenient shared everyday frame.
records.solution_text: Motion is relative. Changing the frame changes the measured position/velocity, not the physical object. Earth’s surface is commonly used because it is stable and shared for everyday locations.
